vocabulary.meaning: money that you owe to another person, bank, or company
examples: Many people use a monthly budget to avoid getting into debt.
It can take several years to pay off a large debt.

vocabulary.meaning: to take money from someone with the intention of paying it back later
examples: She had to borrow money to cover an unexpected expense.
Before you borrow, make sure you understand the repayment terms.

vocabulary.meaning: to have to pay money back to someone
examples: I still owe the bank part of my student loan.
He realised that he owed more money than he had expected.

vocabulary.meaning: to pay back money that you borrowed
examples: They agreed to repay the loan over three years.
It becomes harder to repay debt when interest rates rise.

vocabulary.meaning: extra money paid for borrowing money, usually calculated as a percentage
examples: A high interest rate can make a loan much more expensive.
He chose the bank that offered the lowest interest rate.

vocabulary.meaning: to fail to make required payments at the expected time
examples: He fell behind on payments after losing his job.
Contact the lender early if you think you may fall behind on payments.
